content:
$STRC closing at par isn't a price story. It's a legitimacy story.

---

When a new structured instrument finds its floor on day one, institutions aren't gambling — they're signaling trust in the architecture.

The "Bitcoin treasury company" model just got its first real proof of concept in public markets.

---

The playbook is being written in real time. Other public companies are watching. The ones who move early on this model won't just hold Bitcoin — they'll build capital structures around it.

That's the next frontier. Agree or disagree?
source_story_title: Strategy ($STRC) Closes at Par $100 — Saylor Signals Confidence
source_story_summary: Michael Saylor posted twice about $STRC (Strategy's preferred stock instrument) closing at exactly par value of $100.00, with the cryptic 'Probably Nothing' framing — a well-known crypto meme used to signal that something is actually significant. The double post suggests Saylor views the par close as a meaningful milestone or validation of the instrument's market stability.

content:
Ethereum just admitted L2s alone won't save it.

Glamsterdam isn't an upgrade — it's a strategic correction. Parallel verification and ePBS are Ethereum choosing to compete on performance, not just credibility.

---

The chains that won this cycle were fast and cheap. Ethereum watched. Now it's rebuilding the foundation without burning the house down.

That's harder than launching a new L1. And more important.

---

If ePBS ships cleanly, MEV dynamics shift at the protocol level. That reshapes DeFi incentive structures in ways most teams aren't modeling yet.

Are you auditing your PBS assumptions before Glamsterdam lands? Because that's the work that matters right now.
source_story_title: Vitalik Outlines Ethereum Scaling Roadmap: Glamsterdam Upgrade to Bring Parallel Verification and ePBS
source_story_summary: Vitalik Buterin shared a breakdown of Ethereum's short- and long-term scaling strategy. Key near-term developments include block-level access lists arriving in the Glamsterdam upgrade, which will enable parallel block verification, and enshrined Proposer-Builder Separation (ePBS), also slated for Glamsterdam. These are foundational changes to how Ethereum processes and validates transactions at the protocol level.
